title: Covering by maximal induced bicliques

problem.name_latex: Vertex covering by maximal induced bicliques
problem.name: Vertex covering by maximal induced bicliques
problem.statement_latex:
For a graph $G=(V,E)$ and $k$, decide whether $V$ is the union of $k$ vertex sets, each inducing a maximal complete bipartite subgraph. Maximality means that no extra vertex can be added while preserving this property. The covering is on vertices; overlapping bicliques are permitted. Packing and exact partition variants impose disjointness.
The covering framework uses quantum QRAM time and classical RAM time, while fixed-cover-count algorithms use Boolean bit complexity.

quantum.headline_latex: $O^*(1.8554^n)$, Gaspers--Li biclique covering, packing and partition algorithms.
quantum.details_latex: Maximal induced bicliques admit the restricted enumeration used by the framework, with base $3^{1/3}$. The same theorem handles the three set-family variants once their covering, packing or partition feasibility condition is specified. Coherent preprocessing memory is assumed.

classical.details_latex: For covering by a fixed number $q$ of bicliques, a stronger bound is $\operatorname{poly}(n)2^{O_q(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}$. Two side-membership bits per vertex per biclique impose induced complete-bipartite adjacency through fixed-width clauses, together with a covering clause per vertex. Each covering biclique may be extended to a maximal one, so the encoding decides the formal covering problem. This extension preserves covering and the fixed-$q$ comparison is stated for that variant.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup through a smaller exponential constant for the general family problems with unrestricted part count, using amplitude amplification. Fixed-$q$ covering has the subexponential classical bound.
